- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–2% to align with downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots in the following days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If model forecast is significantly below recent low (e.g., <60% of 30d mean), and sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, consider mean reversion bias — increase forecast toward historical mean by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >3% from model in first 5–7 days, apply a “lag correction” — adjust forecast to match recent 7-day moving average if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model often fails to catch momentum — increase forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
